- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; apply upward bias correction, particularly in early forecast periods.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., 2.25–2.33), producing exaggerated highs in 30d forecast; cap or smooth out overshoots.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d forecasts — if forecast is >2.00 and true outcome drops below 1.00, reduce forecast by 0.3–0.5 units.
- Sentiment history with high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00) correlates with erratic forecasts; use moving average smoothing for 30d horizon.
- If sentiment is positive but price history shows downward trend, model may ignore trend; adjust forecast to reflect recent mean or support level.
- Forecasts with sentiment >0.67 in last 3 days and price >2.00 should be capped at 2.20–2.30 to avoid overestimation.
- If sentiment is low and forecast is high, consider “sentiment-adjusted” correction: subtract 0.1–0.3 from forecast if sentiment <0.40.
